method: Each visible story is a representative first-person reconstruction grounded in the exact Deck Archive title recorded in hidden article metadata. It is not a quotation or a claim that a documented match followed the narrated sequence word for word. Accelerated openings that continue across turns carry a hidden sequence ledger.

stories.title: The last three points were already waiting
stories.story: My opponent went to six and tapped out for Serra Angel , certain the 4/4 flier had bought two turns. I had a Kird Ape in play, a Chain Lightning in hand, and two red mana available. During his end step I cast Lightning Bolt at him, dropping him to three. I untapped, drew another land, and sent the Ape into the Angel. He blocked, expecting to trade the creature for time. I let combat damage clear, then cast Chain Lightning at his face. The Angel was still on the battlefield when his life total reached zero.

stories.title: The new hand never arrived
stories.matchup: Mind Twist Control against five-color Zoo
stories.story: The only card left in my opponent's hand was the one he had just drawn. I had already resolved Mind Twist for four, and The Rack was waiting for his next upkeep. He smiled, tapped three mana, and put Timetwister on the stack. Seven new cards would have erased the whole exchange. I tapped two Islands and cast Counterspell . Timetwister went to the graveyard, his hand stayed empty, and the Rack remained pointed at him. He untapped, took three, drew a single card, and passed without casting it.

stories.title: Three black mana before the first attack
stories.story: A single Swamp was all I showed before casting Dark Ritual . Its three black mana became Hypnotic Specter on turn one. My opponent played a Plains and passed with Swords to Plowshares somewhere in the deck but not in hand. The Specter attacked on turn two and stripped Wrath of God at random. After combat I played a second Swamp and tapped both lands for Hymn to Tourach , taking two more cards. He began his second turn with three cards and no answer to the flier.

stories.title: The Dervish never reached a second counter
stories.matchup: U/W/G Stasis Control against R/G Weenie
stories.story: My opponent's Whirling Dervish had already connected once and picked up its first +1/+1 counter. He added Kird Ape , then moved to combat expecting protection from black to keep the Dervish safe. I let him declare both attackers before tapping Tundra for Swords to Plowshares . The Dervish disappeared, he gained two life, and Old Man of the Sea took the Ape before damage. On my turn I untapped, cast Serra Angel , and left him with more life than before but no creatures and no pressure.

stories.title: The tutor found the missing turn
stories.story: My opponent was at fourteen with no creature in play, but I knew Flash could end the game as soon as he untapped. My Quirion Dryad was already a 5/5, and the cards in hand did not quite make a two-turn clock. I tapped Underground Sea and Mox Jet for Demonic Tutor , found Time Walk , and cast it with Mox Sapphire and Tropical Island . The two blue spells grew the Dryad to 7/7. I attacked, took the extra turn, untapped, and attacked for the remaining seven before my opponent received another draw step.

stories.title: Seven new cards after the hand was spent
stories.matchup: The Perfect Storm against blue control
stories.story: My first six spells left almost nothing in hand: Duress took Force of Will , Black Lotus and Dark Ritual made mana, and two Moxen joined the battlefield. My opponent still had four cards and two untapped lands, but no permission I had seen. I used Mox Ruby for the red mana and cast Wheel of Fortune . The last cards from both hands went to the graveyard and seven fresh ones arrived. Mine contained Yawgmoth's Will , another Dark Ritual, and Tendrils of Agony . I placed the Ritual on the stack while my opponent was still reading the new seven.

stories.title: The artifacts survived the equalizer
stories.matchup: R/W Orb Control against green-white creatures
stories.deckReference: Mark Justice — Pro Tour New York 1996
stories.story: Four creatures faced my empty side of the battlefield, and my opponent still held five cards. I had three lands, Howling Mine , Winter Orb , and one card in hand: Balance . On my turn I cast it, and my hand count was zero and my creature count was zero. He sacrificed every creature, discarded all five cards, and reduced his lands to three. My artifacts stayed exactly where they were. I passed with Howling Mine still feeding the game and Winter Orb allowing only one land back at a time. My opponent untapped a single land, drew two cards, and stared at the empty battlefield he had controlled a minute earlier.

stories.title: The fourth creature made the answer better
stories.matchup: U/W/G Stasis Control against R/G Weenie
stories.story: My opponent already had Kird Ape , Argothian Pixies , and Whirling Dervish in play when he cast a second Ape. I was at eight life and had spent one Swords to Plowshares , so the extra creature looked safe. I untapped Tundra , Savannah , Mox Pearl , and Sol Ring , then cast Wrath of God . All four creatures went to the graveyard at once. He drew for turn, played a land, and passed with nothing to attack. I untapped again with Serra Angel in hand and every permanent that had produced the Wrath still on my side.

stories.title: The Diamonds outlived every land
stories.story: My opponent spent all five lands on a draw spell during his turn and passed still holding Counterspell . I had three lands, including Mishra's Factory , plus Marble Diamond , Sky Diamond , Winter Orb , and Icy Manipulator . I tapped the Marble Diamond for white and all three lands for Armageddon . Every land went to the graveyard, including my Factory. The artifacts stayed. He drew a land and played it, but on his end step my Sky Diamond paid for the Icy to tap it. He turned over the Counterspell and counted the blue sources he no longer had.

stories.title: The Angel became a turn-three attacker
stories.story: My opening hand began with Forest , Birds of Paradise , Fires of Yavimaya , and Blastoderm . The Bird came down on turn one. On turn two it supplied the green mana while two lands cast Fires. My opponent used his second turn for Counterspell mana but let the enchantment resolve. I played a third land, tapped the Bird with the lands, and cast Blastoderm on turn three. Fires gave it haste. The 5/5 attacked immediately, and shroud kept the removal spell in my opponent's hand from touching it. The Bird had turned a four-mana creature into pressure a full turn early.

stories.title: One Elf moved every threat forward
stories.matchup: Fires of Yavimaya against blue-white control
stories.story: Turn one Llanowar Elves made the rest of my hand arrive early. On turn two the Elf and two lands cast Chimeric Idol . On turn three I played Fires of Yavimaya , tapped my lands to animate the Idol, and attacked for three. My opponent spent the next turn holding up Counterspell instead of adding to the board. I made my fourth land drop, used the Elf as the fifth mana for Saproling Burst , and removed three fade counters. Fires gave all three Saprolings haste. Twelve power crossed the table before the control deck had reached its fourth untap.

stories.title: The Angel attacked without opening the door
stories.story: I was at five life when Serra Angel finally untapped. My opponent had Kird Ape and an animated Mishra's Factory , with Lightning Bolt threatening the last points. I attacked for four and left the Angel upright. On his turn he animated the Factory and sent both creatures. Serra Angel blocked the Factory without tapping from its own attack, and Swords to Plowshares removed the Ape before damage. The Factory died in combat. I untapped at five, attacked again, and watched my opponent leave both hands on the table with no creature able to race the vigilant flier.

stories.title: The Dragon made eight damage from nowhere
stories.story: My opponent was at nine behind an empty battlefield and four untapped lands. I drew Shivan Dragon with Birds of Paradise , six lands, and Lightning Bolt available. The Dragon resolved after he used Counterspell on an earlier Howling Mine . On my next combat he had no flier, so Shivan Dragon attacked for five. Before damage I used a Mountain to give it +1/+0, then cast Lightning Bolt after combat. The pumped Dragon and the burn spell accounted for all nine life in one turn. My opponent picked up the Counterspell in his graveyard and looked at the Dragon that had arrived one draw too late to stop.

stories.title: The die found Wrath
stories.matchup: Mind Twist Control against white-blue control
stories.story: Black Lotus became three black mana before my opponent’s first turn, and Hypnotic Specter entered beside Underground Sea and Mox Sapphire . He opened on Tundra and passed. On my second turn I played Island , attacked, and let the Specter’s trigger decide which card left his hand. We turned the cards face down, rolled for one, and Wrath of God went to the graveyard. I tapped the Mox for The Rack and passed with both lands untapped. He played Plains on his second turn and cast Swords to Plowshares at the Specter. I answered with Counterspell . He picked up his remaining hand, counted it once, and passed. On my third turn the Specter crossed the empty sky again.

stories.title: Combat stopped while the Assassin waited
stories.matchup: Mind Twist Control against R/G creatures
stories.story: My Royal Assassin had not destroyed anything yet, but my opponent's combat step had already changed. He controlled Kird Ape and Argothian Pixies , both large enough to pressure my life total. When he tried Control Magic on the Assassin, I used Counterspell . He moved to combat, tapped the Pixies to attack, and I activated Royal Assassin before damage. The Pixies died. On the next turn he looked at the Ape, looked at the untapped Assassin, and passed without attacking. The Rack dealt damage during his upkeep while his best creature remained standing still.

stories.title: The Factory left a counter behind
stories.story: After Nevinyrral's Disk cleared the battlefield, I cast Sengir Vampire into an empty sky. My opponent rebuilt with Mishra's Factory and animated it to block the first attack. The Factory dealt two damage, Sengir dealt four, and the land went to the graveyard. Because the Vampire had damaged the creature that died, it received a +1/+1 counter. On the next turn my opponent cast Swords to Plowshares , but I used Contagion to remove his only other threat before the Vampire left. I gained five life from the enlarged Sengir, and the counter it had earned changed the size of the answer as well as the attack.

stories.title: The Djinn survived the counter war
stories.matchup: Mind Twist Control against white-blue control
stories.story: My opponent cast Serra Angel with two cards left in hand. I used Counterspell , and he answered with his own Counterspell. A second blue pair from Mox Sapphire and Underground Sea let me win the exchange. On my turn Black Lotus supplied the last mana for Mahamoti Djinn , and I passed with two blue lands untapped. On his next turn he tried Control Magic . I countered that too. The 5/6 flier survived the stack fight and began attacking on my following turn while my opponent drew one card at a time looking for another answer.

stories.title: Four green mana paid the impossible upkeep
stories.story: My opponent passed the turn expecting Force of Nature to punish me. The upkeep trigger demanded four green mana, and my lands looked short because one Forest was tapped. I used Llanowar Elves , Fyndhorn Elves , Birds of Paradise , and the untapped Forest to pay all four. Force of Nature remained in play. During combat he blocked the 8/8 with Serra Angel . I cast Giant Growth , making the trampler 11/11. Four damage killed the Angel and seven carried over to my opponent. The creature that was supposed to damage me instead removed his best blocker and most of his life total.

stories.title: The Thrull paid the Lord's price
stories.story: Breeding Pit had already made two Thrull tokens when I drew Lord of the Pit . Five Swamps and Dark Ritual produced the seven mana to cast it. My opponent attacked with Serra Angel on the next turn, then left a smaller flier back to block. At my upkeep the Lord demanded a creature, so I sacrificed one Thrull and kept the 7/7. The remaining token stayed beside Fallen Angel while Lord of the Pit attacked. The small flier absorbed part of the damage, but trample carried the rest across. My opponent moved the blocker to the graveyard and stared at the second Thrull already waiting for the next upkeep.

stories.title: His Dragon left, but mine stayed
stories.story: My opponent tapped six mana for Shivan Dragon and passed with one red source open. I untapped and cast Vesuvan Doppelganger , choosing the Dragon as it entered. He attacked first on the next turn and pumped his original once. I took six, then used Swords to Plowshares on his Shivan Dragon before my own combat. The original disappeared, but the Doppelganger remained a 5/5 flying copy. I attacked with it, then passed with Mana Drain available. His Dragon was gone, and the blue imitation was still on my side of the table.

stories.title: The second Angel created an extra turn
stories.story: One Serra Angel had already attacked my opponent to four when I drew Clone . I cast Clone and chose my own Angel, creating a second vigilant 4/4. The new creature could not attack that turn, so I used Mox Sapphire and Tundra to cast Time Walk . On the extra turn both Angels untapped and attacked together for eight. My opponent used Swords to Plowshares on the original, gaining me four life, but the Clone remained Serra Angel and dealt the last four damage. The copy had entered one turn late and still arrived in time.

stories.title: The Dragon changed sides, then attacked
stories.matchup: Mind Twist Control against red-green creatures
stories.story: My opponent spent six mana on Shivan Dragon and left a Mountain untapped for its pump ability. On my turn I paid four for Control Magic and took the Dragon. He cast Disenchant on the Aura; I used two blue sources for Counterspell , keeping control of the flier. I left the Dragon back and passed. He drew a land and had no further answer. On my following turn the stolen Dragon attacked its former controller for five, and Fireball dealt the remaining damage. His creature crossed the table but never returned.

stories.title: The Orb disappeared before my untap
stories.story: Winter Orb kept three of my lands tapped, but I had left Flood Plain ready from the previous turn. At my opponent's end step I sacrificed the Plain, found a Plains , and spent its white mana on Disenchant . The Orb fell away. On my next untap the locked lands came back. At upkeep I returned an untapped Island to keep Waterspout Djinn ; I replayed it in my main phase. The Djinn attacked for four while three lands remained ready for Dissipate .

stories.title: The blocked Boa still dealt five
stories.story: My opponent was at five and put a 2/2 creature in front of River Boa . The Boa already carried Rancor , so it was a 4/1 with trample. After blockers I cast Giant Growth , raising it to 7/4. Two damage was enough to destroy the blocker, and the remaining five trampled through. He showed me the Counterspell he had kept for Overrun , but combat was already resolving. The one-mana instant had turned an ordinary block into exactly lethal damage.

stories.title: The Ruins became the last point of mana
stories.story: My opponent stabilized at five life with Serra Angel and no cards in hand. I had four Mountains, Dwarven Ruins , and Fireball . The Ruins could have tapped for one red mana, but I sacrificed it for two instead. Together the five lands produced six mana: one red and five for X. I cast Fireball for five damage. Earlier Lightning Bolt and Black Vise had done the rest of the work; the final spell only needed the exact amount. My opponent counted the mana twice, then moved Serra Angel and the rest of the battlefield together into the box.

stories.title: Nineteen life became twenty damage
stories.story: My opening was Taiga , Black Lotus , Channel , and Fireball . I played Taiga, sacrificed the Lotus for three green mana, and spent two of it on Channel. The remaining green mana waited in the pool. I paid nineteen life to Channel for nineteen colorless mana, tapped Taiga for red, and cast Fireball with X equal to twenty. My opponent had not played a land and still held Swords to Plowshares , Serra Angel , and the rest of a perfectly reasonable opening hand. Fireball resolved, and the game ended with me at one life before his first turn.

stories.title: Five cards vanished at random
stories.story: My opponent had rebuilt to five cards behind Land Tax and was holding enough removal to survive the creatures on my side. I tapped four Swamps, used a fifth to cast Dark Ritual , and spent six mana on Mind Twist for five. Every card in his hand was discarded at random, including Swords to Plowshares and Wrath of God . I followed with The Rack and passed. He untapped with no hand, took three damage, drew one card, and found a land. The answer-rich hand he had protected for several turns was gone in a single resolution.

stories.title: The first land never reached turn two
stories.story: My opponent led with Tropical Island and Ponder . I played Swamp , cast Dark Ritual , and used one black mana for Inquisition of Kozilek . The hand showed Brainstorm , Tarmogoyf , and only one additional land. I took Brainstorm, then spent the remaining two black mana on Sinkhole , destroying Tropical Island. He drew for his second turn and found no land to play. On my next turn Wasteland was ready for the second land from his opening hand, while Mishra's Factory waited to become the clock.

stories.title: The Island lasted one turn
stories.deckReference: Brian Kowal and Adrian Sullivan — Original Ponza
stories.story: My opponent opened on Island and passed. I had played Mountain and Mogg Fanatic on turn one; on turn two I added Ancient Tomb . The Tomb and Mountain cast Stone Rain , destroying the Island before Counterspell was available. He played another land and passed. I untapped, used Wasteland on that land, and attacked with Mogg Fanatic. By the time Shard Phoenix joined the battlefield, my opponent had drawn several blue spells and still controlled no mana source capable of casting them.

stories.title: The extra cards became the damage
stories.story: My opponent began the turn at nine life with seven cards in hand. Ebony Owl Netsuke triggered during upkeep and dealt four before the draw step. Two copies of Howling Mine then made him draw three cards. He tapped four mana for Wrath of God , reducing the hand to nine cards. With Wrath still on the stack I cast Sudden Impact . It dealt nine damage, and the game ended before the sweeper resolved. The Mines had looked symmetrical when they entered; on that turn every extra card became another point aimed at their controller.

stories.title: I tapped the prison before my own untap
stories.matchup: R/W Orb Control against midrange creatures
stories.story: Winter Orb had limited my opponent to one land for three turns, but it restricted me too. At the end of his turn I paid one mana and used Icy Manipulator to tap my own Orb. Because the artifact was tapped during my untap step, all four of my lands untapped. I cast Balance , activated Mishra's Factory , and still had mana for Lightning Bolt . Winter Orb untapped with everything else and locked the game again before my opponent's next untap. He untapped one land while I had used a full turn's mana and an animated Factory. The Manipulator had opened the prison only for me.

stories.title: The Disk left one land ready to attack
stories.story: I cast Nevinyrral’s Disk ; it entered tapped, and I passed with Counterspell available. My opponent added a third creature, then cast Control Magic on my Frenetic Efreet , trying to win before the Disk could untap. I countered the Aura; the Efreet stayed on my side. On my turn the Disk untapped. I paid one mana and tapped it, destroying my Efreet along with every other creature, artifact, and enchantment on the table. Mishra's Factory survived as a land. I animated the Factory after the board cleared and sent it across the empty battlefield.

stories.title: Four mana drew the only answer
stories.matchup: U/W Millstone Control against red control
stories.story: I was at three life with four untapped lands and no counterspell in hand. During my opponent's end step I activated Jayemdae Tome , paid four mana, and drew Counterspell . On his next turn he tapped out for Fireball with X equal to three. I used two lands to counter it and kept the other two available for Swords to Plowshares . The following turn Millstone removed two more cards from his library. The Tome had spent an entire turn's mana to draw one card, and that one card was the difference between losing immediately and returning to the control plan.

stories.title: The opening hand dealt damage before combat
stories.story: I used my first Swamp to cast Black Vise and named my opponent. His seven-card hand dealt three damage during the first upkeep. On turn two I cast Dark Ritual into Hypnotic Specter . The Specter connected once, then Hymn to Tourach removed two more cards. Black Vise stopped dealing damage as the hand shrank, but by then it had already turned the keep itself into a liability and helped force my opponent to cast Swords to Plowshares before he wanted to. The artifact had done its work before either player reached the middle game.

stories.title: Two empty-hand triggers ended it
stories.story: My opponent was at six with two cards in hand. Liliana of the Veil made both of us discard; I put Raven's Crime into my graveyard. I then played a land, retraced Raven's Crime, and took his final card. The Rack and Shrieking Affliction were already on the battlefield. At the beginning of his upkeep, The Rack saw zero cards and dealt three. Shrieking Affliction saw one or fewer and dealt three more. He never reached the draw step. The last land in my hand had become the discard spell that turned both permanents on at once.

stories.title: The Ranger found mana inside the lock
stories.story: Winter Orb left my opponent with one untapped land, but my own deck was built to keep moving. I untapped a Forest, tapped Fyndhorn Elves for green, then used Quirion Ranger to return the tapped Forest to my hand and untap the Elf. I replayed the Forest as my land for the turn and used the mana to cast Lhurgoyf . My opponent could not hold up Counterspell and develop the battlefield at the same time. On the next attack, Giant Growth turned the smaller creature he chose to block into a losing exchange while the Orb kept the rest of his lands sideways.

stories.title: The Dragon never untapped again
stories.story: My opponent attacked once with Shivan Dragon and left it tapped. I untapped, cast Meekstone , and passed with Icy Manipulator available. During his next untap step the Dragon's power kept it from untapping. He played another large creature, so I used Icy Manipulator to tap that one before the following untap. Serra Angel attacked from my side and remained untapped because of vigilance, so Meekstone never needed to release it during an untap step. The Dragon stayed sideways for the rest of the game, present on the battlefield but removed from combat by a one-mana artifact.

stories.title: The flip landed on the one card that mattered
stories.story: My opponent had arranged Moat away from the lands and creatures, but it was still the permanent stopping every ground attack. I set Chaos Orb on the table, raised it above the play area, and flipped it. The card turned once and landed across Moat without touching anything else. Moat went to the graveyard. I untapped, cast Ball Lightning , and attacked with it beside Kird Ape . A Giant Growth on the Ape pushed the combat beyond the blockers he had left. The entire board had been organized around one enchantment, and the Orb removed exactly that square of cardboard.

stories.title: The subgame cut five life to two
stories.story: My opponent was at five life in the main game when I cast Shahrazad . We set the main battlefield aside and began the subgame with the cards remaining in our libraries. White Knight held off his early creatures, Swords to Plowshares removed the largest attacker, and Underworld Dreams punished the extra cards he drew while trying to recover. He conceded the subgame rather than play through the lock. We returned to the original table, and Shahrazad made him lose half his life rounded up, dropping five to two. I untapped in the main game and cast Drain Life for the last two.

stories.title: I destroyed the lock only on my turn
stories.story: Kismet made my opponent's new lands enter tapped, and Stasis prevented the old ones from untapping. I paid the blue upkeep for several turns while Howling Mine supplied cards. At the end of his turn I tapped Despotic Scepter to destroy my own Stasis. My untap step returned every land and the Scepter. I drew, replayed a second Stasis, and passed. My opponent had never received an untap step between the two copies because the first enchantment disappeared only after his turn was over. He looked at the tapped lands, then at the new Stasis, and moved directly to drawing a card.
